Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2a) demonstrates asymmetry of the pulmonary hila with a diminutive right hilum and reduced vascular markings in the right lung, which are classic radiographic signs of chronic right pulmonary artery obstruction or hypoplasia associated with Takayasu arteritis. This is confirmed by the axial CT image (Figure 2b), which shows calcification and narrowing of the right pulmonary artery (indicated by the arrow), representing a chronic sequela of the vasculitis rather than an acute embolic event.
